native_result.query: How does the prevalence of non-native plants introduced via gardening vary based on habitat type?
native_result.HypoA: The prevalence of gardening-introduced non-native plants differs between urban/cropland habitats and natural habitats.
native_result.HypoB: Gardening-introduced non-native plants are disproportionately prevalent in low-elevation, human-adjacent habitats (Wetlands 55.8%, Coastal 53.5%, Riparian 36.5%, Urban 29.8% of recorded non-natives) and least prevalent in Croplands (18.5%), against an overall 35.1% gardening share; habitat variation is highly significant (chi2=48.8, df=9, p=1.8e-07; permutation p=0.0005). Forest and Rock outcrop habitats show near-absent gardening share but on 4-8 total species (caveat only). Context: gardening rose to 75.2% of introductions in 1985-2019 vs 16.8% before 1500.
native_result.WorkflowB: 1) Loaded and validated invaded_niche_pathways.csv (632 plots, tab-separated, 0 NAs, no duplicate rows/coordinates; n.gard+n.unint+n.agfo == n.total in all 632 rows; one mutually exclusive habitat label per plot, 10 levels). 2) Built the per-habitat table: plot count, sum n.gard, sum n.total, gardening share with Wilson 95% CIs, and % of plots with >=1 gardening species. 3) Primary test: chi-square of independence on the aggregated habitat x {Gardening, other} species-count table (chi2=48.8, df=9, p=1.79e-07); per-habitat contributions to chi2 reported. 4) Robustness: plot-level permutation test (1999 shuffles of habitat labels among the 191 plots with n.total>0) giving p=0.0005; the unpenalized binomial GLM (n.gard ~ habitat, n.total as trials) diverges due to quasi-complete separation in the tiny forest cells (Broad-leaved 3/3 positive plots 100% gardening; Coniferous 4/5), noted and not pursued per guardrail. 5) Context only, no covariate adjustment (collinear with habitat): temporal contingency table (Gardening share 16.8% -> 75.2% across four periods), species-level cross-check (42/81 gardening-introduced), mean elevation by habitat. Phylogenetic tree inspected (76 tips, 75/81 species mapped) and deemed irrelevant to this question. Executed with python3/pandas/scipy; full output in analysis/output.txt.

sub_hypo.context: Non-native plants introduced through gardening in the Barcelona province, comparing urban/cropland habitats with natural habitats.
sub_hypo.relations: The prevalence of gardening-introduced non-native plants differs between urban/cropland habitats and natural habitats; no direction of difference is specified.

gold_sub_hypo.full_hypo: The prevalence of gardening-introduced non-native plants differs between urban/cropland habitats and natural habitats.

sub_hypo.text: Gardening-introduced non-native plants vary significantly in prevalence among habitats, with shares of 55.8% in Wetlands, 53.5% in Coastal, 36.5% in Riparian, 29.8% in Urban, and 18.5% in Croplands, compared with an overall gardening share of 35.1%.
sub_hypo.context: Non-native plants recorded across 632 plots and 10 habitat types in Barcelona province; the permutation test uses the 191 plots with recorded non-natives.
sub_hypo.relations: Gardening share is sum(n.gard)/sum(n.total) within each habitat. Habitat and gardening versus other introduction pathways are associated (chi-square=48.8, df=9, p=1.79e-07; 1999-shuffle plot-level permutation p=0.0005). Urban and Croplands shares are below the overall share.

sub_hypo.text: Gardening-introduced non-native plants are disproportionately prevalent in low-elevation, human-adjacent habitats.
sub_hypo.context: Habitats in Barcelona province; mean elevation by habitat is contextual only, with no covariate adjustment because elevation is collinear with habitat.
sub_hypo.relations: The hypothesis links greater gardening prevalence to low-elevation, human-adjacent habitat types; an independent elevation effect was not tested.

sub_hypo.text: Forest and Rock outcrop habitats are described as having near-absent gardening shares, but their totals of only 4–8 species warrant caution.
sub_hypo.context: Sparse Forest and Rock outcrop habitat cells in Barcelona province; this is a caveat rather than a robust habitat comparison.
sub_hypo.relations: The hypothesis reports near-zero gardening shares with small denominators. The workflow also reports 100% gardening in 3/3 positive Broad-leaved forest plots and gardening in 4/5 Coniferous forest plots, so the forest characterization is not consistently supported. The habitat binomial GLM diverged owing to quasi-complete separation and was not pursued.

sub_hypo.text: Gardening increased from 16.8% of non-native plant introductions before 1500 to 75.2% in 1985–2019.
sub_hypo.context: Temporal introduction pathways of non-native flora in Catalonia, examined across four periods as context only for the habitat analysis.
sub_hypo.relations: The proportion of introductions attributed to Gardening increased between the earliest and latest periods, from 16.8% to 75.2%; temporal information was not used for covariate adjustment.

Forest and Rock outcrop habitats show near-absent gardening share but on 4-8 total species (caveat only). Context: gardening rose to 75.2% of introductions in 1985-2019 vs 16.8% before 1500.
